messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and increased gateway timeouts for /api/v1/generate in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. 15m error rate: 12% (baseline 0.5%). First observed at 2026-03-14T18:20:34Z. Paging @Sara (oncall).

Sara (oncall): Ack. I'm on it — starting triage. Assigning to SREs: @Mike.

Mike (SRE): Oncall here, looking. Quick checks: health checks to runtime ok, but large spike in 504 gateway timeouts from edge -> runtime proxy. Seeing a surge of long tail latencies from a subset of backend hosts (runtime-rt-??).

Mike (SRE): Trying to fetch runtime proxy logs but traces missing for many requests. Most requests do not have x-trace-id / x-request-id set; makes correlation impossible.

Arjun (runtime): I can confirm — the recent sidecar rollout (envoy v1.22 -> v1.23) dropped header preservation for `x-request-id` for some hostnames. We didn't catch it in canary.

Jess (PM): Customer impact? any high-volume accounts affected?

Mike (SRE): Metric summary: 12 min window shows ~11.8% 5xx overall. Error budget impact: roughly 18k failed requests last 15m. Top impacted product route: /v1/generate (token gen). Top customer fingerprints: cust-acme-inc (approx 24% of failures), cust-beta-co (10%).

Sara (oncall): Prioritize mitigation: 1) restore header propagation & request-id logging; 2) short-term routing fallback to model-variant with lower tail latency; 3) increase runtime pool capacity.

Arjun (runtime): I can push a stopgap envoy patch to force-add `x-request-id` if missing and log it at proxy level. Will also flip runtime log-level for proxy to debug to capture missing context. Patch I will apply: 

```
# kubectl patch envoy filter to add header if missing
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap envoy-sidecar --type=json -p='[{
  "op": "add",
  "path": "/filters/0/typed_config/inserted_request_id",
  "value": {"name":"envoy.filters.http.set_request_headers","typed_config":{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.protobuf.Struct","fields":{"x-request-id":{"kind":{"string_value":"%REQ(:REQUEST_ID)%"}}}}}
}]'
```

Mike (SRE): If we can't restore header propagation quickly we won't be able to trace root cause—do it now. Also I'm going to enable request-level sampling on the tracing side to capture any requests that do have IDs.

Sara (oncall): Do we have a quick runnable command to turn on request-id logging in the runtime service?

Arjun (runtime): Yes — I'll flip `LOG_REQUEST_ID=true` in the runtime config (env var) via a rolling restart of runtime pods. Command: 

```
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/runtime-service LOG_REQUEST_ID=true && kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-service
```

Arjun (runtime): Doing the rollout now. Est. pod restarts: ~6 pods, 3m rolling.

Deploy Bot: rolling restart of deployment/runtime-service started by Arjun (runtime).

Mike (SRE): While that restarts, I recommend a temporary traffic policy: route 30% of traffic from us-west-2 to the lower-latency model-variant (model-v2-quant) to reduce gateway pressure. Creating a runtime routing override now.

Sara (oncall): Go ahead, but limit to 30% to avoid unknown regressions. Monitor error rate.

Mike (SRE): Routing override applied: `route /api/v1/generate -> model-v2-quant (30%)`

Mike (SRE): Quick log excerpt from runtime-proxy prior to restart (raw):

```
[18:18:52] WARN runtime-proxy: upstream timeout after 30s, host=runtime-rt-12, request_id= - , backend_qps=235
[18:18:53] ERROR runtime-proxy: unhandled exception: KeyError('kv_cache') while handling req - no trace id
[18:19:01] WARN runtime-proxy: connection reset by peer
```

Sara (oncall): The missing `request_id` field is annotated as ` - ` above. That matches header drop. Good signal.

Jess (PM): Any ETA on errors dropping after env patch + routing change?

Mike (SRE): Give it one full restart cycle + routing change: 10 minutes. I expect error rate to drop to <2% if header propagation was the main issue; if it doesn't, we have deeper runtime failure.

Arjun (runtime): Rollout finished. Logging shows request ids now being populated for ~85% of incoming requests.

Mike (SRE): Observed 15m error rate now down to 4.1% (from 12%). 1m error rate trending down. Edge gateway errors also dropping. Still seeing residual 5xx from a small subset of hosts.

Sara (oncall): Good. Next stopgap: add a lightweight metric `runtime.request_id_missing` and a tag for host to find remaining bad hosts. I can flip sampling to 100% for 10m to capture traces.

Mike (SRE): Done: `emit.metric('runtime.request_id_missing', 1, tags={'host': host})` injected at proxy level. Also increased tracing sample rate to 100% for 10m.

Deploy Bot: metric toggle and sampling change applied by Mike (SRE).

Mike (SRE): After sampling, we captured full traces for failing requests. Root cause: a race in the KV cache eviction path that manifests under certain concurrent prefix cache invalidations — leads to long tail blocking and upstream timeouts. The envoy header drop made it much harder to correlate which requests hit the bug.

Arjun (runtime): I have a short-term code fix ready to remove the problematic eviction heuristic; will ship a canary to 2 pods, monitor.

Sara (oncall): Ship canary. Keep routing fallback active until we confirm stability.

Arjun (runtime): Canary deployed to runtime-rt-7/8. Monitoring: 2m - no errors on canary. If stable for 8m, I'll promote.

Mike (SRE): Error rate now 0.9% cluster-wide. Canary looks good. Recommend promoting and then ramp down the 30% routing override.

Arjun (runtime): Promoting fix to production now. Rolling deploy.

Sara (oncall): I'm handing over to Mike — I need to step off in 18m. Summary for handoff: 1) root cause KV cache eviction race; 2) missing x-request-id from envoy sidecar worsened troubleshooting; 3) mitigations applied: envoy header patch + LOG_REQUEST_ID, routing fallback 30% -> model-v2-quant, metric and trace sampling increased, canary fix deployed and promoted; 4) customer impact: ~18k failed requests in 15m window, two named customers flagged (cust-acme-inc, cust-beta-co) — sales notified.

Mike (SRE): Taking over. Action items logged: INC-2345. Follow-ups: 1) postmortem (owner: Arjun), 2) remove temporary envoy header patch once all sidecars upgraded to fixed version, 3) add test in canary for header preservation, 4) harden kv cache concurrency (PR in flight).

Jess (PM): Thanks all — I'll coordinate customer comms and open a high-level status note. Please add an ETA for the postmortem in INC-2345.

Mike (SRE): Will do. Also adding a short-term observability improvement: require trace-id propagation on all ingress paths and a nightly job that validates header propagation across versions.

Sara (oncall): Backfill notes into the incident doc and set severity to Sev2. I'll add timeline later.

Incident Bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated by routing fallback + runtime fix. ticket=INC-2345.

Mike (SRE): Final check — error rate stable ~0.6% for 15m. Closing urgent mitigations. Leaving open for postmortem items and follow-ups.

Jess (PM): Closing notes: Sales notified, some customers asked for SLA credits — will follow up with finance. Thanks team.

Mike (SRE): Hand-off complete. If anything regresses, re-alert this thread.
